html_mode_box.1: The Ieon public service (sign up and use) is coming soon. So the two modes don't get mixed, the server won't turn on features that don't match.
html_dev_box.1: Choose whether that PC actually calls the AI and which Codex conversation it continues. In PC mode, change it on the screen opened on that PC; in hub mode, pick the PC on the hub screen (the hub passes it to that PC).
html_cx_box.1: Codex conversations recently used on that PC. Press [Connect] to add one to the allowlist and it appears in the Ieon conversation list right away (same as ＋ Connect conversation on the conversation screen).
html_cls_box.1: Claude conversations a person opened in this cell. Press [Connect] and it appears in the Ieon conversation list right away; questions continue in the same conversation (if a person has Claude open in that folder in the cell, Ieon tells you instead of sending). Usage is billed to the server's Claude login (Settings → Account).
html_cls_list.1: Antigravity conversation and Grok session IDs to continue on that PC. Questions are sent read-only, and usage is billed to each app's login account on that PC. Grok only replies if you have a subscription account.
html_cli_dir.2: Set the folders each AI staff member uses — one personal folder and several shared folders (read-only / read-write). Staff with no folders work exactly as before. Separating folders is not the same as actually blocking access — check "Isolation level" below for each staff member. Folders under the temp folder can't be registered (Codex always allows writing to temp folders, so staff wouldn't be isolated).
html_ws_path.1: Full folder path on that PC (e.g. D:/staff/insurance)
html_ws_edit.2: Choose which account's usage questions are billed to. Conversations (sessions) continue from this PC regardless of the account. The Ieon-only account is separate from your Codex Desktop and web login, and you sign in yourself on the official page (Ieon doesn't read login details). If a limit is hit, Ieon won't switch to another account on its own.
html_ac_sum.1: Sign in whichever way is easier: Log in (ChatGPT subscription — press the button and just approve in "Open approval window"; the code is copied automatically) or API key (enter an OpenAI API key once and Ieon handles the login — billed by usage, for services other people use). Compatible endpoint: keeps Codex as is and sends only the AI model somewhere else (OpenAI Responses API compatible endpoints only — Codex won't accept endpoints that only support Chat Completions). Used only in new Ieon sessions (continuing an existing Codex conversation with another model isn't verified yet). The key isn't shown again, and usage is billed by that service. The default account is used for new sessions and for conversations not set separately below. Shared (shared server) conversations use that server's login.
html_cl_sum.1: Compatible endpoint: keeps Claude Code as is and sends only the AI model somewhere else (e.g. Upstage Solar, a router, a company gateway, a local model on your PC). Enter the Anthropic-compatible address, key, and model name the service gave you. Don't add /v1 at the end of the address (Claude Code appends /v1/messages — confirmed with Upstage on 2026-11-19). The key isn't shown again. Usage is billed by that service.
html_cl_cp_url.1: Address (e.g. https://api.upstage.ai/… — don't add /v1 at the end)
html_cl_code.1: Paste the code you got after approving
html_cl_code.3: Compatible endpoint: keeps Antigravity as is and sends only the AI model somewhere else (a company gateway, a router, a local model on your PC) — this is Antigravity's "enterprise model gateway" feature. Enter an https address (http://localhost works for your own PC), the key, the model names to use (comma-separated; leave empty for the list the gateway provides), and the request format (usually Gemini). The key isn't shown again.
html_gk_key_cancel.1: Today's questions and this month's tokens for each account. Limits apply only to API key accounts (no limit by default). Once exceeded, Ieon doesn't send with that account and tells you (it won't resend automatically).
html_ac_usage.2: You opened this with a "PC connection link" made on the hub screen. Once connected, questions sent from that hub run on this PC. Connect only if you made the link yourself.
html_hub_link_box.1: Connects this PC to a hub when you use hub mode (ieun). The easiest way is to open the hub screen's "PC connection link" on this PC. To do it manually, enter the hub address and press "Connect" to get a 6-digit code, then approve the same code under Hub settings → Apps and devices → Devices → Connection requests.
html_hl_forget.2: Pick a bot to enter the bot token from the messenger in the "Token" field below. Saved tokens aren't shown again, and the bot connects within 1 minute.
html_b_users.1: Messenger user IDs, comma-separated (added to the common allowlist)
html_b_delete.2: Recent messages (24 hours) sent to the bot by people not on the allowlist. Press "Allow" to add them as extra allowed users for that bot.
html_denied_rows.2: If a value is saved here, it's used; otherwise the value set during installation is used. Press "Use file value" to clear the value here and go back to the installation value.
html_skill_box.1: Paste this address into the URL field of your Kakao Open Builder skill. It contains a secret path, so don't post it anywhere else.
html_kk_reset.2: Register Codex conversations and Claude channel sessions that already exist on a PC. Sessions added during installation are view-only. A Codex conversation must also be on that PC's Settings → This PC allowlist to actually run (on this PC, "＋ Connect conversation" on the conversation screen does both at once). To show it to a bot, pick it under "Visible existing sessions" in the bot editor.
html_bd_ref.1: Codex conversation ID (UUID) / ieon for Claude channel
html_ns_reset.1: The number of questions (waiting + in progress) one PC or engine cell handles at once. Beyond that, Ieon doesn't queue them; it replies "busy" and won't resend automatically. 0 means no limit.
html_hl_per_host.1: Questions one device handles at once
html_hl_per_host.2: Approval card: in work mode, when the engine asks for permission and there's no answer within this time, it's denied (15–1440 minutes = 24 hours). While waiting, that conversation stays on hold. Stay signed in: after this period you sign in again (1–90 days).
html_login_days.2: Sends a question to AI staff at set times (e.g. every day at 9:00, "Summarize yesterday's changes"). The AI is called while nobody is around, so you confirm when creating or turning it back on. It only sends questions (conversations in work mode are skipped at that time), there's a daily limit, and if a question with an unknown result remains, the schedule stops (turn it back on to resume). Replies collect in that conversation.
html_r_guide.1: Added before the first question of new sessions created by this role's bot
html_my_msg_section.1: You can also use your conversations through this hub's messenger bots (Telegram, Discord, Slack, LINE, KakaoTalk). Get a number and send it to the bot as is to link it to your account (10 minutes, one use). A linked messenger account shows only your conversations.
html_my_pw_section.1: Change the password you use to sign in to this screen (10+ characters). Changing it signs you out everywhere else.
html_dv_section.1: A new PC connects right away if you open the "PC connection link" above on that PC. Or press "Connect" under that PC's Ieon settings → Apps and devices → Hub connection, and it appears under "Connection requests" below. Check that it matches the 6-digit code on the PC screen, then approve. Ieon exchanges the tokens for you. PC safety settings (allowlist, real runs, work folder) can't be changed here.
html_invite_box.1: Open this link on the PC you want to connect: that PC's Ieon settings screen opens and you just press "Connect" (no code check). It works once within 10 minutes. Ieon must be installed on the PC.
html_sec_src.1: Choose where this hub's web can be opened from. It opens if any one rule passes. Changes that would block where you're connected from now aren't saved. Your current address:
html_inst_box.1: Makes a command to paste into the terminal of another Linux server to install Ieon there. It downloads the installer from this hub and starts the installation (no repository access needed). The command works for 1 hour only and disappears when the hub restarts. Don't send it to anyone else.
html_mu_box.1: When on, a "Sign-up request" option appears on the sign-in screen. Applicants can use it only after you approve them here, and each connects only their own PC and sees only their own conversations (admins can't see others' conversations either). For others to reach this hub, you also need to open the access restriction above. Empty or 0 means no limit. To set it per person, use the "Limit" column in the table (empty follows the default, 0 means no limit for that person only). Today counts from midnight Korea time; once exceeded, questions aren't sent and the user is told (admins have no limit). Members agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy when signing up.
html_hcx_box.1: To create new Codex sessions on the hub, this hub must be signed in to Codex with your ChatGPT account. Press "Log in" to get an address and a code; open the address, enter the code, and approve. "Device code login" must be turned on in your ChatGPT security settings.
html_hub_live.2: Issue a key here to let a program you made send questions to Ieon. The key is shown only once when issued, so put it in that program's settings right away. Choose the sessions each program can see, and revoke the key when it's no longer needed.
html_app_key_hide.2: Get the Ieon App from this server (no app store). Type this server's address followed by /app in your phone browser's address bar and the Android app downloads right away. On first install, your phone asks once to allow "apps from unknown sources".
html_app_dl.1: Connects the Ieon App on your phone or PC to this server. Make a code and enter it in the app with the server address — the code works once within 10 minutes. The app handles conversations, rooms, cards, and approvals; settings are changed only on this web screen.
html_ad_list.1: Even with the app closed, "○○ replied" arrives on your phone (question and reply text are not sent). Just upload the two files from the Firebase console here — no need to open or copy them. The private key isn't shown again after upload.

server_lang.title: Server language
server_lang.tip: Language for messenger bot replies, Kakao notices, headers added for the AI, and texts the server makes (such as account labels). Each person picks their own screen language at the top. The first value is the language of the PC or server it was installed on.
bot_lang.label: Reply language
bot_lang.tip: Language this bot uses for replies, help and approval prompts. Leave it empty to follow "Server language" in Admin. Questions and AI answers are not translated.
